messages.content: Find me a documentary about global warming.

function.name: retrieve_scientific_paper
function.description: Fetches the details of scientific research paper based on its topic. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

year.description: Year of publishing of the research paper. If not specified, fetches the most recent paper

author.description: Author of the research paper. If not specified, fetches the paper with most citations

message.content:
Here are a few highly regarded documentaries that explore global warming and climate change:

| Title | Year | Synopsis | Where to Watch |
|-------|------|----------|----------------|
| **An Inconvenient Truth** | 2006 | Former Vice‑President Al Gore presents a compelling case for urgent action against climate change, using data, personal anecdotes, and visual graphics. | Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Google Play |
| **An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power** | 2017 | A follow‑up to the original film, this sequel examines progress (or lack thereof) since 2006 and highlights new scientific findings and policy developments. | Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Google Play |
| **Before the Flood** | 2016 | Leonardo DiCaprio travels around the world to meet scientists, activists, and policymakers, documenting the impacts of climate change and potential solutions. | Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, iTunes |
| **The 11th Hour** | 2007 | Produced by Leonardo DiCaprio, this film features interviews with leading environmentalists and scientists, offering a global perspective on the planet’s ecological crisis. | Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Google Play |
| **Our Planet** (Series) | 2019–present | While not solely focused on climate change, this nature series showcases how human activity threatens biodiversity and ecosystems, underscoring the urgency of addressing global warming. | Netflix |
| **Climate Change: The Facts** | 2018 | A short, science‑based documentary that explains the science behind climate change, its impacts, and what can be done to mitigate it. | YouTube (official channel), Vimeo |

These films are widely available on major streaming platforms and offer a mix of scientific explanation, personal narrative, and calls to action. If you’re looking for something more academic or research‑focused, let me know and I can pull up a recent scientific paper on the topic.
